p: Bretton is on the west side of the city, which makes it handy for one of Peterborough's best green spaces. Ferry Meadows in Nene Park is just a short drive away, with lakes, meadows, cycle paths and plenty of room for a picnic. It's a lovely way to stretch your legs after the skates come off, and kids love the play areas. The Nene Valley Railway also runs heritage steam trains through the park area, which is a treat for anyone who likes their days out with a bit of nostalgia.

Back at the rink, a few basics will set you up for a good session. Get your skates fitted snugly, with the laces pulled tight around the ankle. Wear gloves, long socks and something you can move in. Take your first few laps near the barrier and don't be afraid to hold on. Confidence comes quicker than you'd expect.

If you're skating with little ones, keep them close and stay on the outside of the ice where it's a bit calmer. A skating aid, where available, gives them something to lean on while they learn. And don't forget a snack for afterwards, because skating is surprisingly hungry work.

Plenty of skaters who start out wobbling at public sessions end up taking lessons and loving it. If your crew gets the bug, Peterborough's long history of skating means there's a well-established scene to grow into.
